name: James
summary: A brother of Jesus, named among His family in His hometown. He later became a leader of the church in Jerusalem, one of the men Paul said were seen as pillars.

key_moments.title: Seen by the Risen Lord
key_moments.description: Paul wrote that after Christ rose from the dead, He was seen by many, and then by James.

key_moments.title: Tells the Council Not to Trouble the Gentiles
key_moments.description: When the apostles and elders met about the Gentiles, James answered them. He said they should not trouble Gentiles who turn to God, but write to them to keep away from idols, sexual sin, strangled animals and blood.

key_moments.title: Gives Paul the Right Hand of Fellowship
key_moments.description: Paul went up to Jerusalem and saw James, the Lord's brother. Later James, Cephas and John gave Paul and Barnabas their right hands as a sign of fellowship.

key_moments.title: Writes to the Twelve Tribes
key_moments.description: James wrote a letter to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, calling himself God's servant.
